title: 《高等微積分》第 58 集｜序列緊緻性｜Loomis & Sternberg 第 4 章 §4
description:
本集是 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》第 4 章第 4 節（書頁 205 到 209）。書頁 209 到 210 是習題 4.1 到 4.16。

先把子序列說清楚：從一個序列裡挑出無窮多項，按原來的順序排好。接著是一條看起來很怪的引理：如果每一支子序列都還有一支收斂到某一點，那麼整個序列就收斂到那一點。理由是，如果不收斂，就挑得出一整支每一項都離那點至少 ε 遠的子序列，而那一支的任何子序列也收斂不到。

定義：一個子集是序列緊緻的，如果它裡面每一個序列都有子序列收斂到它裡面的一點。書上的話很傳神：這裡等於是無中生有地造出收斂。引理 4.2 說這樣的集合一定又閉又有界。定理 4.1 說連續映射把緊緻集送成緊緻集，而實數線上的緊緻集含著最大與最小元，合起來就是那條熟悉的推論：連續函數在緊緻定義域上取得到最大與最小值。

定理 4.2 說連續的雙射若定義域緊緻，反函數也連續——證明正是用剛才那條怪引理。緊緻這個假設不能省：把零到二 π 那一段（不含右端）繞成一個圓，映射連續而且是雙射，可是反函數在一那一點不連續。

接下來證實數線上的有界閉集是緊緻的。引理 4.3：有界的單調序列收斂。引理 4.4：任何實數列都有單調子序列，用的是峰項——大於等於它後面所有項的那些項。峰項有無窮多個的話它們本身就是遞減的一支；只有有限多個的話，最後一個之後挑得出嚴格遞增的一支。合起來就是定理 4.3。定理 4.4 用歸納推到 n 維，定理 4.5 隨即得到。

最後補上第 3 章欠的那個洞。定理 4.6：n 維實空間上所有範數等價。一個方向是三角不等式直接給的；另一個方向是把任意範數限制到一範數的單位球面上，那是緊緻集，所以最小值取得到而且不是零。第 3 章第 4 節當時用了這個事實卻沒有工具證它，到這裡才補上。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 58 | Sequential Compactness | Ch. 4, §4
description:
This episode is section 4 of chapter 4, pages 205 to 209, of Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus. Pages 209 to 210 are exercises 4.1 to 4.16.

First subsequences: pick infinitely many terms out of a sequence, keeping their order. Then a lemma that sounds unlikely: if every subsequence has a further subsequence converging to a point, the whole sequence converges to it. The reason is that a sequence failing to converge admits a whole subsequence staying at least epsilon away, and no subsequence of that one converges either.

The definition: a subset is sequentially compact if every sequence in it has a subsequence converging to a point of it. The book puts it well — here we create convergence out of nothing. Lemma 4.2 says such a set is closed and bounded. Theorem 4.1 says continuous maps carry compact sets to compact ones, and a compact subset of the line contains its largest and smallest elements; together they give the familiar corollary that a continuous function on a compact domain attains its extremes.

Theorem 4.2 says a continuous bijection with compact domain has a continuous inverse, and its proof is exactly where that odd lemma earns its place. Compactness cannot be dropped: wrap the interval from zero to two pi, right end excluded, around a circle, and the map is continuous and bijective while the inverse is not continuous at one point.

Then bounded closed sets on the line. Lemma 4.3: a bounded monotone sequence converges. Lemma 4.4: any real sequence has a monotone subsequence, via peak terms, the terms at least as large as everything after them. Infinitely many peaks already form a decreasing subsequence; only finitely many, and past the last one a strictly increasing subsequence can be built. Together that is Theorem 4.3. Theorem 4.4 lifts it to n dimensions by induction, and Theorem 4.5 follows.

Finally the gap left in chapter 3 is filled. Theorem 4.6: all norms on real n-space are equivalent. One inequality falls out of the triangle inequality; the other restricts an arbitrary norm to the unit sphere of the one-norm, which is compact, so a minimum is attained and cannot be zero. Section 4 of chapter 3 used that fact without the tools to prove it, and here it is proved.

Part of a bilingual animated teaching series (English edition).
